blocks.text: Conclusion: US PE recovered in 3Q26 — deal value +20.9% QoQ, exit value +50.4% QoQ — but the recovery is top-heavy: mega-exits are 73.3% of year-to-date exit value and the middle market only 28.9%. Capital has rotated from software (IT 15.0% of deal value, 27.9% in 2025) to energy (17.7%). For new commitments we favour the middle market and managers one size below the largest. Blue Owl GP Stakes V gained 1.4% in the quarter to 30 Jun 2026 with DPI flat at 0.4x: “recovering marks, no new cash”.

items: Software out, energy in: software deal value US$17.7bn, -83.7% YoY; energy 17.7% of year-to-date deal value against 7.1% in 2025.
Exits rebounded through large sales to corporates: US$86.6bn of 3Q26 disclosed exit value went to corporate acquirers; median exit US$715.0m.
Sponsors lost M&A share: buyout/LBO was 31.8% of global M&A value in Q1–Q3 against 41.6% in 2025, the lowest since 2016.
Rates rose: a 25bp increase in September; the syndicated market refinanced a record US$11.8bn of direct loans.
Middle market gained share: 51.0% of buyout value (43.4% in 2025) and 52.7% of buyout fundraising.

rows: Corporate megadeals led the first half; sponsor share 31.8%
Add-ons are 74.9% of buyout count; more, smaller deals
Mega-exits 73.3% of the year's value; backlog still building

About one year of deal value; not an overhang
Ahead on deals, returns and fundraising; exits are the weak link

items: Fee stream supported: capital is going to established managers (step-up 1.44x); management fees are 25.4% of GPS V's cumulative gross distributions.
Carry and distributions slow: exits are concentrated in a few large sales; sale proceeds are 7.8% of distributions and DPI is flat at 0.4x.
Marks volatile: CVC +11.5% on its share price and Bitkraft -38.2% on fundraising; MBK (-24.9% since inception) unchanged.
